subjects.assignment: Draw a picture representing the birth or ministry of Jesus and tell its story at home.

subjects.subject: Islamic Studies
behavioralObjectives: state the main Islamic teaching in simple words
identify important terms or examples
show respectful conduct connected with the lesson.
subjects.instructionalMaterials: Qur’an, Arabic letter or topic cards, pictures, audio recitation where suitable, board and marker.
subjects.lessonContent: The Articles of Faith are core beliefs in Islam. At Basic 1 level, learners are introduced to belief in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and Allah’s decree. The lesson emphasises sincere belief and good conduct.
subjects.teacherLearnerActivities: Teacher introduces each article using simple language and visual cards. Learners repeat the names, match each belief with a simple description, and discuss respectful behaviour.
subjects.evaluation: Name the Articles of Faith introduced in the lesson.
subjects.assignment: Learn the six Articles of Faith and tell a parent what each means in simple words.

subjects.subject: Civic Education
behavioralObjectives: explain the civic idea in simple words
identify responsible behaviour connected with the topic
demonstrate respect, cooperation or responsibility.
subjects.instructionalMaterials: picture cards, posters, flashcards, board and marker, simple role-play materials.
subjects.lessonContent: A good citizen is honest, respectful, responsible, peaceful, helpful and willing to obey reasonable laws. Good citizens care for people and property, tell the truth and contribute positively to their community.
subjects.teacherLearnerActivities: Teacher uses character cards to discuss good and poor choices. Learners sort qualities into positive behaviours and act out one example of responsible citizenship.
subjects.evaluation: Mention five qualities of a good citizen.
subjects.assignment: Choose three good-citizen qualities and explain how you can practise them.

subjects.subject: Social Studies
behavioralObjectives: explain the social concept simply
identify examples from family or community life
demonstrate a positive social value or behaviour.
subjects.instructionalMaterials: family/community pictures, charts, flashcards, board and marker, role-play cards.
subjects.lessonContent: Culture is the way of life of a people. It includes language, food, dressing, music, dance, greetings, beliefs, festivals, occupations and customs. Culture is learned and shared across generations.
subjects.teacherLearnerActivities: Teacher shows pictures of Nigerian cultural practices. Learners identify examples of language, food, clothing, music or festivals from their communities.
subjects.evaluation: What is culture? Mention four parts of culture.
subjects.assignment: Draw or describe one cultural practice in your family or community.

subjects.subject: Security Education
behavioralObjectives: explain the security concept simply
identify a possible risk or protective measure
choose a safe response and know when to tell a trusted adult.
subjects.instructionalMaterials: safety posters, warning-sign cards, pictures, flashcards, board and marker.
subjects.lessonContent: Security gadgets are devices used to help protect people and property. Examples include alarms, locks, security lights, cameras and access-control devices. Children should understand their purpose without attempting to operate restricted equipment without adult supervision.
subjects.teacherLearnerActivities: Teacher shows pictures of security devices and explains their uses. Learners match each device to the protection it provides.
subjects.evaluation: Name four security gadgets and state one use of each.
subjects.assignment: Draw two security gadgets and write their uses.

subjects.subject: Vocational Education
behavioralObjectives: identify the vocational concept or item
state its use or importance
demonstrate safe and responsible work habits.
subjects.instructionalMaterials: real tools or pictures, occupation cards, household objects, charts, board and marker.
subjects.lessonContent: Musical instruments are objects used to produce music. Examples include drums, keyboard, guitar, recorder, flute, maracas and xylophone. Instruments can be grouped by how they produce sound, but at Basic 1 level learners focus on recognising and naming familiar instruments.
subjects.teacherLearnerActivities: Teacher plays or demonstrates simple instruments where available. Learners identify the sound or picture and copy simple rhythm patterns by clapping.
subjects.evaluation: Name five musical instruments and identify one instrument that can be beaten to make sound.
subjects.assignment: Draw two musical instruments and write their names.

subjects.subject: Home Economics
behavioralObjectives: identify the body part or hygiene practice
explain why care is important
demonstrate or describe safe personal-care habits.
subjects.instructionalMaterials: body charts, hygiene items, pictures, flashcards, board and marker.
subjects.lessonContent: The mouth helps us eat, speak and taste. Good mouth care includes brushing the teeth, rinsing after meals, drinking clean water and avoiding excessive sugary foods. Children should report mouth pain or sores to an adult.
subjects.teacherLearnerActivities: Teacher uses a mouth chart and demonstrates healthy mouth-care habits. Learners identify good and poor habits.
subjects.evaluation: Mention three uses of the mouth and three ways to care for it.
subjects.assignment: Write five habits that help keep the mouth healthy.

subjects.subject: Agricultural Science
behavioralObjectives: identify the agricultural concept or examples
state one or more uses or characteristics
show safe and responsible attitudes toward plants or animals.
subjects.instructionalMaterials: plant or animal pictures, real samples where safe, charts, flashcards, board and marker.
subjects.lessonContent: Commercial use means using plants to produce goods that can be sold or used in business. Crops such as cocoa, oil palm, rubber, cotton, rice, cassava and maize may provide raw materials, food or products for markets and industries.
subjects.teacherLearnerActivities: Teacher displays products made from crops. Learners match each crop with a familiar product and discuss why crops are economically useful.
subjects.evaluation: What is a commercial use of a plant? Mention four crops with commercial value.
subjects.assignment: Find three plant products sold in a market and identify the plant they come from.

subjects.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
behavioralObjectives: explain the artistic idea in simple language
identify examples
participate in a creative activity using simple materials.
subjects.instructionalMaterials: drawing paper, pencils or crayons, picture cards, simple art/craft materials, board and marker.
subjects.lessonContent: Teamwork means working together to achieve a common goal. Good teamwork involves listening, taking turns, sharing materials, helping others and respecting different ideas. Art projects often require teamwork.
subjects.teacherLearnerActivities: Teacher gives a simple group drawing or rhythm task. Learners share materials, take turns and complete the activity together.
subjects.evaluation: What is teamwork? Mention four behaviours that show good teamwork.
subjects.assignment: Do one simple group task at home and explain how you worked together.

subjects.subject: Yoruba Language
behavioralObjectives: recognise and pronounce the target Yoruba words or expressions
connect words with familiar objects, numbers or pictures
use the language in simple oral practice.
subjects.instructionalMaterials: Yoruba alphabet/vocabulary cards, pictures, real objects, number cards, board and marker.
subjects.lessonContent: Isorongbesi activities develop learners’ ability to hear, repeat and use simple Yoruba expressions appropriately. The teacher introduces short, familiar expressions and guides learners to repeat them with correct pronunciation and meaning.
subjects.teacherLearnerActivities: Teacher models short expressions and explains when they are used. Learners repeat chorally and individually, then use them in simple classroom exchanges.
subjects.evaluation: Repeat three expressions correctly and explain or demonstrate their use.
subjects.assignment: Practise three expressions with a family member.

subjects.subject: Igbo Language
subjects.topic: Kwu Nid A Nwere Udaelu, Ndi Nke Ozo Nwere Udale
behavioralObjectives: recognise the target Igbo letters, words or expressions
pronounce them with guidance
use the new language in a simple oral activity.
subjects.instructionalMaterials: Igbo alphabet/word cards, pictures, real objects, board and marker, textbook.
subjects.lessonContent: This lesson focuses on listening for different vowel or sound qualities in Igbo and recognising the sound patterns demonstrated by the teacher. Learners practise careful listening, repetition and matching sound with written forms.
subjects.teacherLearnerActivities: Teacher models the target sounds in clear pairs and uses simple words. Learners listen, repeat and identify which sound they hear.
subjects.evaluation: Repeat the target sounds and identify the correct example from two choices.
subjects.assignment: Practise the target sounds and words aloud.

subjects.subject: French Language
behavioralObjectives: recognise the target French vocabulary
pronounce the words with guidance
use the vocabulary in a simple oral response.
subjects.instructionalMaterials: French word cards, number or colour cards, pictures, audio recording if available, board and marker.
subjects.lessonContent: Les couleurs means colours in French. Common beginner colours include rouge (red), bleu (blue), jaune (yellow), vert (green), noir (black), blanc (white) and orange. Learners connect each French word to a coloured object or picture.
subjects.teacherLearnerActivities: Teacher displays coloured objects and says each French colour. Learners repeat, point to the correct colour and practise short phrases such as “rouge” or “un objet rouge.”
subjects.evaluation: Name five colours in French and identify them on a colour chart.
subjects.assignment: Colour seven objects and label the colours in French.

subjects.subject: History
behavioralObjectives: explain the historical idea simply
identify people, places or sources connected to the topic
state why the lesson is important for understanding the past.
subjects.instructionalMaterials: old photographs or pictures, family tree/chart, map or place pictures, story cards, board and marker.
subjects.lessonContent: Art has different branches, such as visual art, music, drama and dance. Studying these branches helps historians understand how people in different periods expressed ideas, beliefs and daily life. Examples may include traditional musical instruments, clothing patterns, sculpture, painting and storytelling.
subjects.teacherLearnerActivities: Teacher shows examples and asks learners what each reveals about a people or period. Learners classify the examples by art branch.
subjects.evaluation: Name four branches of art and give one example of each.
subjects.assignment: Draw one traditional art example from your community.

subjects.subject: Verbal Reasoning
behavioralObjectives: identify the verbal reasoning pattern
apply the pattern to simple examples
give accurate answers and explain the rule in simple words.
subjects.instructionalMaterials: letter cards, word cards, picture cards, worksheet, board and marker.
subjects.lessonContent: Familiar words are common words children meet often in speech, books and daily life. Learners recognise, read and use words such as boy, girl, book, home, school, sun, food and play. Repeated practice builds vocabulary and reading fluency.
subjects.teacherLearnerActivities: Teacher uses word cards and pictures. Learners match words to pictures, read the words aloud and use selected words in short phrases.
subjects.evaluation: Read ten familiar words and match five of them to pictures.
subjects.assignment: Write ten familiar words and read them aloud to a parent or guardian.

subjects.subject: Quantitative Reasoning
behavioralObjectives: understand the quantitative relationship
solve simple examples using objects or numbers
show the steps or reasoning clearly.
subjects.instructionalMaterials: counters or bottle tops, number cards, number line, worksheet, board and marker.
subjects.lessonContent: Addition means putting quantities together to find a total. Learners combine objects, count on and write simple number sentences. Early work should use numbers within the learners’ current range.
subjects.teacherLearnerActivities: Teacher demonstrates addition with counters and a number line. Learners combine groups, count on and write the matching number sentence.
subjects.evaluation: Solve 3+2, 4+1, 5+3 and 6+2 using objects or mental counting.
subjects.assignment: Solve ten simple addition questions.

subjects.subject: English Language
subjects.topic: Blending Sounds of Letters to Form Words
behavioralObjectives: identify and explain the key idea in the lesson
use the new language skill in simple examples
respond correctly to simple oral and written questions.
subjects.instructionalMaterials: flashcards, picture cards, word cards, board and marker, textbook.
subjects.lessonContent: Blending means joining individual letter sounds to make a word. For example, /c/ + /a/ + /t/ becomes cat. Learners practise simple consonant-vowel-consonant words such as cat, bat, sun, pen and dog.
subjects.teacherLearnerActivities: Teacher models slow sound blending, then increases the speed. Learners tap or point to each letter, say the sounds, and blend them into whole words.
subjects.evaluation: Blend the sounds in c-a-t, p-e-n, s-u-n and d-o-g. Read the completed words.
subjects.assignment: Practise reading ten three-letter words.

subjects.subject: Mathematics
behavioralObjectives: identify and explain the number concept
solve simple examples using concrete materials and numerals
write or state answers correctly.
subjects.instructionalMaterials: number cards, counters or bottle tops, number chart, board and marker, exercise book.
subjects.lessonContent: Counting skill involves saying numbers in the correct sequence, counting objects accurately once each, and matching the final count to the quantity. Learners practise one-to-one counting and simple number recognition.
subjects.teacherLearnerActivities: Teacher uses objects, claps and steps for counting practice. Learners count aloud, touch each object once, and record the final number.
subjects.evaluation: Count groups of objects and write the total for each group.
subjects.assignment: Count five different groups of household objects and record the totals.

subjects.subject: Basic Science
behavioralObjectives: explain the key science idea in simple language
identify familiar examples
relate the lesson to everyday life and safety.
subjects.instructionalMaterials: real objects, picture charts, flashcards, simple demonstration items, board and marker.
subjects.lessonContent: Energy is the ability to make things happen or do work. Children experience energy when they move, play, hear sounds, see with light, feel heat and use electrical appliances. Common forms and sources discussed at this level include heat, light, sound and movement. Safety is important when using sources of energy.
subjects.teacherLearnerActivities: Teacher demonstrates simple examples such as light from a torch, sound from clapping, heat from the sun and movement during play. Learners identify the type or source of energy in each example.
subjects.evaluation: Give three examples of energy in everyday life and identify the source or form in each case.
subjects.assignment: Find three examples of energy use at home and write what the energy helps you do.

subjects.subject: Information Technology
behavioralObjectives: identify the computer concept or part
state its simple use or purpose
demonstrate safe handling or basic use where appropriate.
subjects.instructionalMaterials: computer set, keyboard and mouse, computer charts, flashcards, board and marker.
subjects.lessonContent: A keyboard is an input device used to enter letters, numbers and commands into a computer. Important keys for beginners include letter keys, number keys, the Spacebar, Enter and Backspace. Learners practise locating keys and typing short words.
subjects.teacherLearnerActivities: Teacher shows a keyboard and points out common keys. Learners locate keys, type their names or simple words, and practise using Spacebar and Backspace.
subjects.evaluation: 1. What is a keyboard used for? 2. Name three keys. 3. Which key makes a space between words?
subjects.assignment: Draw a simple keyboard and label the Spacebar, Enter and Backspace keys.

subjects.subject: Physical and Health Education (P.H.E.)
behavioralObjectives: describe the movement or physical-skill concept
perform the skill with simple control
observe basic safety and fair-play rules.
subjects.instructionalMaterials: soft balls or bean bags, cones or markers, open play area, whistle if available, water for hydration.
subjects.lessonContent: Sports and games are organised physical activities that help the body become strong and healthy. Simple Basic 1 activities may include running, ball games, hopping, jumping, relay play and throwing games. Learners practise fair play, turn-taking and following simple rules.
subjects.teacherLearnerActivities: Teacher explains one or two simple games, demonstrates the rules, and organises learners in small groups. Learners participate, take turns and practise teamwork.
subjects.evaluation: Name three sports or games and state one rule for safe play.
subjects.assignment: Ask a parent or guardian to name two traditional or modern games played in your community.

subjects.subject: Christian Religious Studies (C.R.S.)
behavioralObjectives: state the main Bible teaching in simple words

subjects.teacherLearnerActivities: Teacher asks short review questions, retells selected stories, shows pictures and leads learners in recall activities. Learners answer orally, retell key ideas and complete a short revision exercise.
subjects.evaluation: Use oral and written revision questions covering the term’s major topics.
subjects.assignment: Revise the term’s Bible lessons and learn one key sentence from each major topic.

subjects.subject: Islamic Studies
subjects.topic: Prophets of Allah in the Qur’an
behavioralObjectives: state the main Islamic teaching in simple words
identify important terms or examples
show respectful conduct connected with the lesson.
subjects.instructionalMaterials: Qur’an, Arabic letter or topic cards, pictures, audio recitation where suitable, board and marker.
subjects.lessonContent: Islam teaches that Allah sent prophets to guide people. Learners are introduced to familiar prophets named in the Qur’an, such as Adam, Nuh (Noah), Ibrahim (Abraham), Musa (Moses), Isa (Jesus) and Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon them). Prophets taught people to worship Allah and live righteously.
subjects.teacherLearnerActivities: Teacher displays names or pictures on cards and briefly introduces selected prophets. Learners match names with simple facts and repeat the lesson respectfully.
subjects.evaluation: Name four prophets and state the common message they taught.
subjects.assignment: Write five names of prophets mentioned in the lesson.

subjects.subject: Social Studies
subjects.topic: Values That Show Bad Morals in Our Society
behavioralObjectives: explain the social concept simply
identify examples from family or community life
demonstrate a positive social value or behaviour.
subjects.instructionalMaterials: family/community pictures, charts, flashcards, board and marker, role-play cards.
subjects.lessonContent: Bad morals are behaviours that are harmful, dishonest, disrespectful or unfair. Examples include stealing, lying, fighting, bullying, destroying property and insulting others. Learners are encouraged to recognise these behaviours and choose better alternatives.
subjects.teacherLearnerActivities: Teacher uses simple scenarios to show bad and better choices. Learners identify what is wrong and suggest a respectful alternative.
subjects.evaluation: Mention four examples of bad morals. Give a better behaviour for one of them.
subjects.assignment: Write three bad behaviours children should avoid and the good behaviours that can replace them.

subjects.subject: Security Education
behavioralObjectives: explain the security concept simply
identify a possible risk or protective measure
choose a safe response and know when to tell a trusted adult.
subjects.instructionalMaterials: safety posters, warning-sign cards, pictures, flashcards, board and marker.
subjects.lessonContent: Personal security means taking reasonable steps to protect yourself from harm. Children should stay with trusted adults, use safe routes, avoid isolated places, keep personal information private, and report threats or unwanted contact immediately to a trusted adult.
subjects.teacherLearnerActivities: Teacher discusses safe and unsafe scenarios such as being approached by a stranger or getting lost. Learners practise saying “no,” moving to a safe place and seeking a trusted adult.
subjects.evaluation: Mention five personal-security rules for children.
subjects.assignment: Write the names of three trusted adults you can contact for help.

subjects.subject: Vocational Education
behavioralObjectives: identify the vocational concept or item
state its use or importance
demonstrate safe and responsible work habits.
subjects.instructionalMaterials: real tools or pictures, occupation cards, household objects, charts, board and marker.
subjects.lessonContent: Furniture includes movable household items used for sitting, sleeping, storing or working. Examples include chairs, tables, beds, cupboards, shelves and sofas. Furniture should be used carefully and kept clean and in good condition.
subjects.teacherLearnerActivities: Teacher shows pictures or classroom furniture and asks learners to name each item and describe its use.
subjects.evaluation: Name five pieces of furniture and state one use of each.
subjects.assignment: Draw two pieces of furniture used in your home.

subjects.subject: Home Economics
behavioralObjectives: identify the body part or hygiene practice
explain why care is important
demonstrate or describe safe personal-care habits.
subjects.instructionalMaterials: body charts, hygiene items, pictures, flashcards, board and marker.
subjects.lessonContent: The eyes help us see. Eye care includes reading in good light, keeping hands clean before touching the face, avoiding dangerous objects near the eyes, wearing recommended protective eyewear, and telling an adult when there is pain or difficulty seeing.
subjects.teacherLearnerActivities: Teacher discusses good and poor eye-care habits using pictures. Learners identify safe practices and demonstrate a good sitting distance for reading.
subjects.evaluation: What do we use our eyes for? Mention four ways to care for the eyes.
subjects.assignment: Write five eye-care rules.

subjects.subject: Agricultural Science
subjects.topic: Types of Farm Animals (Based on Habitat)
behavioralObjectives: identify the agricultural concept or examples
state one or more uses or characteristics
show safe and responsible attitudes toward plants or animals.
subjects.instructionalMaterials: plant or animal pictures, real samples where safe, charts, flashcards, board and marker.
subjects.lessonContent: Farm animals can be grouped by habitat, meaning where they live. Some live mainly on land, such as goats, sheep, cattle and chickens. Others live in water, such as fish. Some animals can live around both land and water environments depending on the species.
subjects.teacherLearnerActivities: Teacher displays habitat pictures and animal cards. Learners place each animal in the most suitable habitat group and explain the choice.
subjects.evaluation: Group five farm animals according to their main habitat.
subjects.assignment: Draw two land farm animals and one water farm animal.

subjects.subject: Yoruba Language
behavioralObjectives: recognise and pronounce the target Yoruba words or expressions
connect words with familiar objects, numbers or pictures
use the language in simple oral practice.
subjects.instructionalMaterials: Yoruba alphabet/vocabulary cards, pictures, real objects, number cards, board and marker.
subjects.lessonContent: Picture identification helps learners name familiar people, animals, objects and actions in Yoruba. Learners look at each picture, say what they see and listen for the correct word.
subjects.teacherLearnerActivities: Teacher displays pictures one at a time. Learners identify, pronounce and repeat the Yoruba names and answer simple questions about the pictures.
subjects.evaluation: Identify and name five pictures in Yoruba.
subjects.assignment: Draw three familiar objects and write or say their Yoruba names.

subjects.subject: French Language
behavioralObjectives: recognise the target French vocabulary
pronounce the words with guidance
use the vocabulary in a simple oral response.
subjects.instructionalMaterials: French word cards, number or colour cards, pictures, audio recording if available, board and marker.
subjects.lessonContent: Le corps means the body. Learners are introduced to simple body-part vocabulary such as la tête (head), les yeux (eyes), les oreilles (ears), le nez (nose), la bouche (mouth), les mains (hands) and les pieds (feet).
subjects.teacherLearnerActivities: Teacher points to body parts and says the French words. Learners repeat, point to their own body parts and play a simple “show me” game.
subjects.evaluation: Name five body parts in French and point to each one.
subjects.assignment: Draw a person and label five body parts in French.

subjects.subject: History
subjects.topic: Important Places of History in Lagos State
behavioralObjectives: explain the historical idea simply
identify people, places or sources connected to the topic
state why the lesson is important for understanding the past.
subjects.instructionalMaterials: old photographs or pictures, family tree/chart, map or place pictures, story cards, board and marker.
subjects.lessonContent: Lagos State contains places associated with important parts of Nigerian history and culture. Examples learners may encounter include the National Museum Lagos, Freedom Park, Tafawa Balewa Square and other heritage sites. Such places help preserve memories, objects and stories from the past.
subjects.teacherLearnerActivities: Teacher shows pictures or a simple map of selected Lagos heritage sites. Learners identify the places and discuss why historical sites should be protected.
subjects.evaluation: Name three important historical or heritage places in Lagos State and state why such places matter.
subjects.assignment: Draw or describe one historical place in Lagos State that you would like to visit.

subjects.subject: Verbal Reasoning
behavioralObjectives: identify the verbal reasoning pattern
apply the pattern to simple examples
give accurate answers and explain the rule in simple words.
subjects.instructionalMaterials: letter cards, word cards, picture cards, worksheet, board and marker.
subjects.lessonContent: Familiar words are common words children meet often in speech, books and daily life. Learners recognise, read and use words such as boy, girl, book, home, school, sun, food and play. Repeated practice builds vocabulary and reading fluency.
subjects.teacherLearnerActivities: Teacher uses word cards and pictures. Learners match words to pictures, read the words aloud and use selected words in short phrases.
subjects.evaluation: Read ten familiar words and match five of them to pictures.
subjects.assignment: Write ten familiar words and read them aloud to a parent or guardian.

subjects.subject: Quantitative Reasoning
behavioralObjectives: understand the quantitative relationship
solve simple examples using objects or numbers
show the steps or reasoning clearly.
subjects.instructionalMaterials: counters or bottle tops, number cards, number line, worksheet, board and marker.
subjects.lessonContent: Subtraction means taking away or finding how many are left. Learners begin with real objects, remove some items and count what remains. The written subtraction sign is introduced with simple examples.
subjects.teacherLearnerActivities: Teacher demonstrates taking away counters. Learners remove objects, count the remainder and write simple subtraction sentences.
subjects.assignment:
Solve ten simple subtraction questions within the numbers taught.
